Independent current judgment: WEAK. RFC 4271 Section 5 says: "If a path with a recognized, transitive optional attribute is accepted and passed along to other BGP peers and the Partial bit in the Attribute Flags octet is set to 1 by some previous AS, it MUST NOT be set back to 0 by the current AS." The five current positive covers supply meaningful preservation evidence at distinct boundaries; they do not establish every applicable default transformation or forwarding path. The summary has no matching single-positive annotation, and the two required owner-terminal classification rulings remain unissued. No polarity authorization or whole-row credit follows from these observations.

The two COMMUNITY component covers are TestRFC4271PartialFromPreviousASNotCleared and TestRFC4271PartialFromPreviousASNeverCleared. The core test preserves already-E0 recognized COMMUNITY and unknown250 with zero fresh stamps. The reactor test requires successful enforcement, ActionNone and parsed recognized COMMUNITY/unknown251 flags; its unnegotiated empty-AS_PATH fixture is component publication rather than external Session admission. Full receipts job-rfc4271-legacy-recognized-community-proof-3c250514.log and job-rfc4271-legacy-reactor-community-preserve-proof-8288f460.log show clean package passes of 0.284s and 0.771s. Their COMMUNITY-only clearing fault produces only the recognized E0-versus-C0 nonfatal assertion, with later unknown-attribute checks continuing. Neither root proves exact attribute values or recipient delivery.

TestReceivedPartialSurvivesOrdinarySessionWire receives valid eBGP routes, retains and selects them, then checks ordinary iBGP Session output with four-octet ASNs on both sessions. Its four recognized attributes are AGGREGATOR, COMMUNITY, EXTENDED_COMMUNITY and LARGE_COMMUNITY; literal values, useful IPv4 NLRI and every observed announcement are checked. Clean initial output and destination reconnect without another source UPDATE pass. Receipt job-rfc4271-partial-session-wire-proof-0813db6c.log records both clean children passing, package 9.431s. The final-private-buffer Partial-clearing fault leaves the complete twin passing and makes the partial child fail at its first AGGREGATOR flag assertion after useful/value controls. Later partial-target, history, counter, reconnect and final-store assertions are skipped. No independently broken reconnect-only behavior, each-target fault or foreign acceptance is claimed.

TestAggregatorPartialSurvivesASPathRebuild preserves all ten original complete/Partial and narrow/widen/unchanged-width cases, including protocol-prepend controls. The real ASPathEdit generator and default rebuild must preserve borrowed input, both NLRI sections, useful attributes, absent AS4 companions and exact projected AGGREGATOR value before its flags assertion. Receipt job-rfc4271-aggregator-component-proof-268be5a1.log shows all ten clean children passing, package 1.038s. Omitting only generic Partial inheritance makes exactly the three Partial width-change children fail at final flags, E0 versus C0; seven controls pass, package 0.892s.

TestPrefixSIDPartialSurvivesNextHopCleanup preserves all eight original complete/Partial, mixed, unknown-only, Service-only and unchanged-hop cases. It reaches the configured next-hop decision, automatic Service-TLV removal and specialized default handler. Valid framing, useful route/next hop, source immutability and exact retained non-Service TLVs precede final flags. Receipt job-rfc4271-prefix-sid-component-proof-66d69129.log shows all eight clean children passing, package 0.935s. Omitting only specialized Partial inheritance makes exactly the two Partial surviving-TLV children fail at final flags, E0 versus C0; six controls pass, package 0.890s. Neither component fault causes skips or other diagnostics, and neither supplies Session/socket evidence.

All five canonical discrimination records are current in job-rfc4271-partial-five-cover-freshness-8f08e193.log; stale and unproven are empty. This establishes recorded-cover freshness, not whole-row conformance or audit fingerprint freshness. All 46 legacy code bindings remain, supplemented by 11 bindings for the new fixture/assertion helpers, AS-width intent/generators, default registration/rebuild, specialized cleanup, next-hop decisions and TLV/framing fixtures. These 57 bindings preserve the actual evidence dependencies. Explicit operator attribute updates, transparent route-server behavior and legal whole-attribute suppression remain supported. Unknown-only preservation belongs to RFC4271-5-3; complete twins are software controls, not a claim that Section 5 requires every complete path to be accepted.
